cohort: The study included 931 women aged 18 to 45 with a low-risk, term pregnancy, who delivered between June 2008 and April 2012 at a University Hospital in Bogota, Colombia.
finding: Among low-risk pregnant women, cesarean delivery on maternal request (CDMR) was associated with a lower rate of adverse maternal outcomes, adverse neonatal outcomes, and newborn hospitalization compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery on maternal request (CDMR) was associated with a lower rate of adverse perinatal outcomes when compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery in low-risk pregnancies.
